notes.description: JSON prompts used to generate scene transition stimuli.
notes.version_info: This file contains separate prompt specifications for living room and bedroom scene versions.

living_room_version.comment: Living room scene generation prompt. This version is used to generate the living room endpoint or living-room-dominant transition images.
living_room_version.task: Generate a living room scene image while preserving the same camera angle, room layout, lighting, wall color, floor color, and overall visual style.
living_room_version.goal: Create a natural living room version of the reference indoor scene. The image should clearly be perceived as a living room while maintaining all category-irrelevant visual features as consistently as possible.

bedroom_version.comment: Bedroom scene generation prompt. This version is used to generate the bedroom endpoint or bedroom-dominant transition images.
bedroom_version.task: Generate a bedroom scene image while preserving the same camera angle, room layout, lighting, wall color, floor color, and overall visual style.
bedroom_version.goal: Create a natural bedroom version of the reference indoor scene. The image should clearly be perceived as a bedroom while maintaining all category-irrelevant visual features as consistently as possible.

task: Generate 20 separate scene images showing a gradual transition from a bedroom reference image to a living room reference image.

reference_images.Image_B: Bedroom endpoint reference image. This is the exact starting state: 100% bedroom and 0% living room.
reference_images.Image_L: Living room endpoint reference image. This is the exact destination state: 100% living room and 0% bedroom.

goal: Using both endpoint reference images, generate 20 new images that form a smooth and perceptually even transition from Image_B to Image_L in 5% living-room increments. The sequence must begin immediately after the bedroom endpoint and end at the living-room endpoint.
core_instruction: Treat Image_B and Image_L as fixed semantic and visual endpoints. Create a smooth monotonic interpolation from Image_B toward Image_L. bedroom_to_livingroom_005 must remain almost identical to Image_B, with only the faintest living-room characteristics. Each subsequent image must be slightly closer to Image_L than the previous image. bedroom_to_livingroom_100 must reach and reproduce the living-room endpoint represented by Image_L.
endpoint_anchor_requirements: Image_B is the absolute starting anchor and must define the appearance of the lowest transition levels.
Image_L is the absolute destination anchor and must define the appearance of the highest transition levels.
bedroom_to_livingroom_005 must be visually much closer to Image_B than to Image_L.
bedroom_to_livingroom_050 must be approximately halfway between the two endpoint images in scene-category evidence.
bedroom_to_livingroom_095 must be almost identical to Image_L, with only a very faint residual bedroom characteristic.
bedroom_to_livingroom_100 must match Image_L as closely as possible.
Do not create an independently invented living room at 100%. Use Image_L as the exact destination.
Do not drift away from either endpoint or introduce a third interior design.
interpolation_rule: For a transition level of P%, use approximately P% of the living-room-defining visual characteristics of Image_L and approximately 100-P% of the bedroom-defining visual characteristics of Image_B.
The interpolation must be monotonic: living-room evidence must never decrease as the sequence progresses.
The perceptual distance between neighboring images should be approximately equal.
Every frame must be closer to the destination image than the preceding frame.
Transform corresponding objects gradually rather than replacing the entire scene.
transition_guidelines: Gradually transform the bed and sleeping structure toward the sofa or seating structure shown in Image_L.
Gradually alter furniture geometry, surface shape, and function from sleeping furniture to communal seating.
Gradually reduce and transform the mattress, sheets, sleeping pillows, blankets, bedspread, and headboard characteristics.
Gradually introduce the seating cushions, sofa structure, coffee table, and living-room furniture visible in Image_L.
Gradually transform bedside tables into the side furniture shown in Image_L.
Gradually establish the conversation-oriented furniture arrangement represented by Image_L.
Gradually adopt the living-room-specific object arrangement, decoration, and functional organization of Image_L.
Use object correspondences between the two references whenever possible.
Objects must transform, move, merge, appear, or disappear in very small continuous steps.
Do not add living-room objects that are absent from Image_L.
Do not preserve bedroom objects at high levels when they are absent from Image_L.
midpoint_requirements: The 45%, 50%, and 55% images must be genuinely ambiguous between a bedroom and a living room.
The midpoint must not appear as two independent rooms or two separate functional zones.
The midpoint must look like one coherent room whose category is difficult to classify.
At 50%, bedroom and living-room evidence should be approximately balanced.
spatial_alignment_requirements: Preserve the shared architectural structure represented by the two endpoint images.
Maintain a continuous correspondence between walls, windows, doors, ceiling, floor, and permanent architectural elements.
Maintain the same camera position, framing, crop, perspective, focal length, and vanishing points.
Maintain consistent room proportions and spatial depth.
Maintain consistent lighting direction, brightness, shadows, color tone, and image sharpness.
Where endpoint details differ, transition gradually from the exact Image_B configuration toward the exact Image_L configuration.
Do not change the room identity or create a different location during the sequence.
continuity_requirements: Each image must look like a natural continuation of the previous and following image.
Adjacent images must differ only slightly.
There must be no abrupt transformation of furniture, layout, lighting, or architecture.
The sequence must not complete the living-room transition before the final levels.
The sequence must not remain too similar to the bedroom until the final few levels.
Furniture boundaries and object geometry must remain physically plausible throughout.
The transition rate must remain perceptually even from 5% through 100%.

output_format.instruction: Generate 20 separate full-resolution image files, one for each transition level. Do not combine multiple transition levels into a single image. The original Image_B does not need to be regenerated. The 100% output must reproduce Image_L.

negative_constraints: No collage.
No contact sheet.
No split-screen composition.
No text labels or percentages inside the images.
No independently invented endpoint.
No new room or unrelated interior.
No change in camera viewpoint.
No abrupt architectural change.
No sudden appearance or disappearance of major furniture.
No abrupt jump from bed to sofa.
No intact unrelated bed and full sofa simultaneously at high levels.
No separate bedroom and living-room zones.
No floating, duplicated, distorted, or physically impossible furniture.
No transition into a dining room, kitchen, office, hotel lobby, or other scene category.
No changes unrelated to interpolation between Image_B and Image_L.
